arxiv-1705-04538.title: Ionic selectivity and filtration from fragmented dehydration in multilayer graphene nanopores
arxiv-1705-04538.creator: Subin Sahu, Michael Zwolak
arxiv-1705-04538.description: Abstract Selective ion transport is a hallmark of biological ion channel behavior but is a major challenge to engineer into artificial membranes. Here, we demonstrate, with all-atom molecular dynamics simulations, that bare graphene nanopores yield measurable ion selectivity that varies over one to two orders of magnitude simply by changing the pore radius and number of graphene layers.

arxiv-2106-14607.title: Faulhaber’s Formula, Odd Bernoulli Numbers, and the Method of Partial Sums Thanks: This work is licensed under the CC BY 4.0, a Creative Commons Attribution License.
arxiv-2106-14607.creator: Ryan Zielinski
arxiv-2106-14607.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Ryan Zielinski. Let “Faulhaber’s formula” refer to an expression for the sum of powers of integers written with terms in n(n+1)/2. Initially, the author used Faulhaber’s formula to explain why odd Bernoulli numbers are equal to zero. Next, Cereceda gave alternate proofs of that result and then proved the converse, if odd Bernoulli numbers are equal to zero then we can derive Faulhaber’s formula.

arxiv-2205-04880.title: Consensus based optimization via jump-diffusion stochastic differential equations
arxiv-2205-04880.creator: D. Kalise, A. Sharma, M.V. Tretyakov
arxiv-2205-04880.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by D. Kalise, A. Sharma, M.V. Tretyakov. We introduce a new consensus based optimization (CBO) method where interacting particle system is driven by jump-diffusion stochastic differential equations. We study well-posedness of the particle system as well as of its mean-field limit. The major contributions of this paper are proofs of convergence of the interacting particle system towards the mean-field limit and convergence of a discretized particle system towards the continuous-time dynamics in the mean-square sense.

arxiv-2302-00396.title: Unrestricted quantum moduli algebras, III: Surfaces of arbitrary genus and skein algebras
arxiv-2302-00396.creator: Stéphane Baseilhac 1 , Matthieu Faitg 2 , Philippe Roche 3
arxiv-2302-00396.description: Abstract . We prove that the quantum moduli algebra associated to a possibly punctured compact oriented surface and a complex semisimple Lie algebra 𝔤 \displaystyle\mathfrak{g} is a Noetherian and finitely generated ring; if the surface has punctures, we prove also that it has no non-trivial zero divisors.

arxiv-2304-04365.title: Reflection Vectors and Quantum Cohomology of Blowups
arxiv-2304-04365.creator: Todor MILANOV and Xiaokun XIA
arxiv-2304-04365.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Todor MILANOV and Xiaokun XIA. Let X X be a smooth projective variety with a semisimple quantum cohomology. It is known that the blowup Bl pt ⁡ ( X ) \operatorname{Bl}_{\rm pt}(X) of X X at one point also has semisimple quantum cohomology. In particular, the monodromy group of the quantum cohomology of Bl pt ⁡ ( X ) \operatorname{Bl}_{\rm pt}(X) is a reflection group.

arxiv-2304-09784.title: Zero-Knowledge MIPs using Homomorphic Commitment Schemes
arxiv-2304-09784.creator: Claude Crépeau, John Stuart
arxiv-2304-09784.description: Abstract A Zero-Knowledge Protocol (ZKP) allows one party to convince another party of a fact without disclosing any extra knowledge except the validity of the fact. For example, it could be used to allow a customer to prove their identity to a potentially malicious bank machine without giving away private information such as a personal identification number.

arxiv-2310-03275.title: Power Optimization in Multi-IRS Aided Delay-Constrained IoVT Systems
arxiv-2310-03275.creator: Baolin Chong, Hancheng Lu, Langtian Qin, Chenwu Zhang, Jiasen Li, Chang Wen Chen
arxiv-2310-03275.description: Abstract With the advancement of video sensors in the Internet of Things, Internet of Video Things (IoVT) systems, capable of delivering abundant and diverse information, have been increasingly deployed for various applications. However, the extensive transmission of video data in IoVT poses challenges in terms of delay and power consumption.

arxiv-2502-10863.title: Enhancing catalyst activity of two-dimensional C 4 N 2 through doping for the hydrogen evolution reaction
arxiv-2502-10863.creator: Bruno Ipaves, João F. Justo, James M. de Almeida, Lucy V. C. Assali, Pedro Alves da Silva Autreto
arxiv-2502-10863.description: Abstract This study investigates the structural, electronic, and catalytic properties of pristine and doped C 4 N 2 nanosheets as potential electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction. The pristine C 36 N 18 nanosheets exhibit limited HER activity, primarily due to high positive Gibbs free energies ( > > 2.2 eV).

arxiv-2503-00625.title: Perceptual Visual Quality Assessment: Principles, Methods, and Future Directions
arxiv-2503-00625.creator: Wei Zhou 1 , Hadi Amirpour 2 , Christian Timmerer 2 , Guangtao Zhai 3 , Patrick Le Callet 4 , Alan C. Bovik 5 1 Cardiff University, UK 2 University of Klagenfurt, Austria 3 Shanghai Jiao Tong University, China 4 University of Nantes, France 5 University of Texas at Austin, USA Email: zhouw26@cardiff
arxiv-2503-00625.description: Abstract As multimedia services such as video streaming, video conferencing, virtual reality (VR), and online gaming continue to expand, ensuring high perceptual visual quality becomes a priority to maintain user satisfaction and competitiveness. However, multimedia content undergoes various distortions during acquisition, compression, transmission, and storage, resulting in the degradation of experienced quality.

arxiv-2503-03057.title: Interacting mesons as degrees of freedom in a chiral model
arxiv-2503-03057.creator: Rajesh Kumar, Joaquin Grefa, Konstantin Maslov, Yuhan Wang, Arvind Kumar, Ralf Rapp, Claudia Ratti, Veronica Dexheimer
arxiv-2503-03057.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rajesh Kumar, Joaquin Grefa, Konstantin Maslov, Yuhan Wang, Arvind Kumar, Ralf Rapp, Claudia Ratti, Veronica Dexheimer. We study the equation of state of hot and dense hadronic matter using an extended Chiral Mean Field (CMF) model framework where the addition is the inclusion of interactions of thermally excited mesons. This is implemented by calculating the in-medium masses of pseudoscalar and vector mesons, obtained through the explicit chiral symmetry-breaking and vector interaction terms in the Lagrangian, respectively, prior to applying the mean-field approximation.

arxiv-2506-12032.title: Embedding Trust at Scale: Physics-Aware Neural Watermarking for Secure and Verifiable Data Pipelines Generalizable Lessons for Enterprise Workflows
arxiv-2506-12032.creator: Krti Tallam
arxiv-2506-12032.description: Abstract We present a robust neural watermarking framework for scientific data integrity, targeting high-dimensional fields common in climate modeling and fluid simulations. Using a convolutional autoencoder, binary messages are invisibly embedded into structured data such as temperature, vorticity, and geopotential.

arxiv-2510-03462.title: Single-Spin Nitrogen-Vacancy Magnetometer with Enhanced Static Field Sensitivity
arxiv-2510-03462.creator: Vinaya K. Kavatamane, Dewen Duan, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Manh-Huong Phan, Gopalakrishnan Balasubramanian
arxiv-2510-03462.description: Abstract Precision sensing and imaging of weak static magnetic fields are crucial for a variety of emerging nanoscale applications. While nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond provide exceptional AC magnetic field sensitivity with nanoscale spatial resolution, their sensitivity to static (DC) magnetic fields is fundamentally limited by the short dephasing time ( T 2 ∗ \text{T}_{2}^{*} ) due to spin-spin interactions.

arxiv-2511-11059.title: Generalizing quantum dimensions: Symmetry-based classification of local pseudo-Hermitian systems and the corresponding domain walls
arxiv-2511-11059.creator: Yoshiki Fukusumi, Taishi Kawamoto
arxiv-2511-11059.description: Abstract We study conformal field theories (CFTs) and their classifications from a modern perspective based on the abstract algebraic formalism of symmetries or conserved charges, known as symmetry topological field theories (SymTFTs). By studying the algebraic structure of the SymTFTs in detail, we found a natural generalization of the quantum dimensions associated with (pseudo-)Hermitian systems and (non)-unitary CFTs.

pmc-12375084.title: Quantum secured blockchain framework for enhancing post quantum data security
pmc-12375084.creator: Nalavala Ramanjaneya Reddy, Supriya Suryadevara, K. Guru Raghavendra Reddy, Ramisetty Umamaheswari, Ramakrishna Guttula, Rajitha Kotoju
pmc-12375084.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Quantum computing is an evolution of classical computing, capable of solving problems that are competitive enough to break the existing cryptographic primitives upon which current blockchain systems are based. Popular schemes like RSA, ECDSA, and SHA-256 can be compromised by quantum algorithms (Shor’s and Grover’s), raising questions about the security and trustworthiness of blockchain-based applications in finance, healthcare, and supply chains.

pmc-12468807.title: Comparison of Narrow (<3.75 mm) and Standard (≥3.75 mm) Diameter Implants Supporting the Same Multiple Fixed Prostheses and Mirroring Real-World Clinical Scenarios: Non-Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-12468807.creator: Eduardo Anitua, Ander Alcaine, Mohammad Hamdan Alkhraisat
pmc-12468807.description: Objective: To compare the survival of narrow (<3.75 mm) implants and standard diameter (≥3.75 mm) implants supporting the same multiple fixed prostheses and mirroring real-world clinical scenarios. Methods: This is a controlled clinical trial where both test (diameter < 3.75 mm) and control (diameter ≥ 3.75 mm) implants supported the same prosthesis.

pmc-13175142.title: New medical schools in Sub-Saharan Africa –a cross-sectional survey of educational structures, operations, and policies
pmc-13175142.creator: Krish Shah, Elizabeth S. Rose, Andrew Rees, Seun Falayi, Quentin Eichbaum
pmc-13175142.description: Introduction:Africa does not have enough doctors despite having the highest continental burden of disease. Encouragingly, many new medical schools are opening and have begun to graduate doctors. However, the educational structures, operations, and policies of these schools remain poorly understood. This study aimed to better understand these dimensions of new medical schools on the continent.

pmc-13221090.title: Associations of Normalization and Regularization with Machine Learning Overfitting in Cross-dataset Classification of Deaths Using Transcriptomic and Clinical Data: A Secondary Analysis of Publicly Available Databases
pmc-13221090.creator: Fei Deng, Lanjing Zhang
pmc-13221090.description: Background and objectives:Normalization can standardize and improve machine learning (ML) performance on omics data. However, it is unclear whether normalization is associated with overfitting (i.e., worse cross-dataset performance than intra-dataset performance). Therefore, we aimed to examine associations of normalization and regularization with overfitting of ML on omics data.

pmc-13312697.title: Transposable elements in hematopoietic stem cells upon aging and myeloid malignancies
pmc-13312697.creator: Emilie Elvira-Matelot, Françoise Porteu
pmc-13312697.description: Transposable elements (TEs) constitute nearly half of the human genome and profoundly influence hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) biology. In this review, we synthesize current evidence demonstrating that TEs exert dual and context-dependent roles in HSCs during steady-state hematopoiesis, stress responses, aging, and leukemogenesis.

pmc-13313401.title: Nested PCR detection of JC polyomavirus large T-antigen in prostate cancer tissues: a case–control analysis in a Sudanese population
pmc-13313401.creator: Maria Ahmed Mohamed Higair, Babbiker Mohammed Taher Gorish, Sana Eltahir Abdallah
pmc-13313401.description: BackgroundThe potential involvement of JC polyomavirus (JCPyV) in prostate cancer (PCa) remains a subject of debate, as existing in vitro studies have produced conflicting results. Understanding the viral oncogenic mechanisms underlying prostate cancer could offer valuable insights into its etiology.

pmc-13585318.title: Targeted community screening in areas of high socioeconomic deprivation enhances the detection of liver fibrosis
pmc-13585318.creator: Huw F. Purssell, Stephanie R. Landi, Alexander A. Warner-Levy, Lucy R. Bennett, Jennifer A. Scott, Christopher E. Mysko, Deepankar Gahloth, Oliver E. Street, Indra Neil Guha, Neil A. Hanley, Karen Piper Hanley, Varinder S. Athwal
pmc-13585318.description: Background:Risk-factor-based community screening has been used to identify early liver disease. Risk-factor prevalence and liver-related outcomes are significantly affected by socioeconomic deprivation. However, the impact on targeted community screening is unknown. We evaluated the influence of deprivation on fibrosis detection within a population screening pathway.

pmc-13700373.creator: Martin H Ruwald, Martin Haugdal, Christian Jøns, Rene Worck, Christina Alhede, Arne Johannessen, Uffe Gang, Niels Sandgaard, Xu Chen, Morten Lock Hansen, Peter Karl Jacobsen, Jim Hansen
